Subject: Pilot SLOs & residency requirement for Suncrest POC

Neha —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. Our engineering lead reviewed the flow and we have two hard asks for the upcoming pilot (we hope to start first week of September):

- Model residency: we need a pinned model instance / residency for the pilot tenant so token KV cache can remain hot (expected QPS ~45 req/s peak).
- Latency SLO: 50ms p95 for single-turn generation (100–200 tokens typical).

I've attached the updated SOW and a small latency/profile dump from our side. Procurement wants confirmation that these are feasible before we sign. If full 50ms p95 isn't realistic, let us know the trade-offs and whether a dedicated pool or reserved capacity option is required.

Happy to jump on a quick call today if helpful.

—Sam

Team — forwarding Suncrest's ask. Key bullets:
- Customer: Suncrest Health (DEAL-1587) wants a 3-month pilot starting early Sept.
- Requirements: pinned model residency for the tenant + 50ms p95 single-turn generation (~100–200 tokens).
- Load: expected peak ~45 req/s, typical median prompt length ~120 tokens.
- Attachments: SOW + their latency dump. HubSpot link + DocuSign referenced below.

Ask for Product/Eng: please advise ASAP on feasibility and fastest path to satisfy the SOW language (they need this answered for procurement). Specifically:
1) Can we offer model residency/pinning in a way that guarantees hot KV cache for the tenant for the duration of the pilot? What infra config is required (dedicated pool size, reserved capacity, node types)?
2) Can we meet 50ms p95 with our hosted offering, or only with a Dedicated deployment? If not 50ms, what is a realistic p95 and what engineering work (quantization, custom kernels, shorter context windows) would be required to hit 50ms?
3) Proposed timeline: we need a recommended plan and a go/no-go for committing in the SOW by EOD Aug 25. If a short spike is required, what's the minimal two-week spike scope and deliverables (test harness, perf targets)?

Links: https://hubspot.example/crm/deal/1587 (customer record), DocuSign: https://docusign.example/suncrest/sow_v3

Please reply in-thread with estimates and blockers so I can respond to Suncrest and update procurement language.

—Neha
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Suncrest: pilot scope & SLO ask — need feasibility + ETA

Neha / team — quick feasibility readout after a 30m sync with infra folks:

Summary: We can meet the "residency" requirement via a short-term Dedicated pool (reserved nodes pinned to the tenant) and by enabling aggressive KV prefix caching. For latency: 50ms p95 for 100–200 token outputs is aggressive on general-purpose hardware; expected p95 for a tuned path with 8-bit quantization and dedicated pool is ~55–65ms. Hitting 50ms reliably requires either:
  - very narrow model variant (smaller param count, pruned tokenizer) OR
  - custom low-latency kernel tuning + colocated NVLink cluster (higher cost).

Proposed minimal plan (spike):
- Week 1 (by Aug 29): configure a 2-node dedicated test pool, enable 8-bit quant profile, seed KV cache with representative prefixes, run synthetic replay of their sample traces. Deliverable: perf report + optimized config that shows p50/p95.
- Week 2 (by Sep 5): iterate on kernel params, measure end-to-end with their traces, and produce suggested SOW language (what we can guarantee and what is advisory).

Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- Residency: node-level tenancy for pilot tenant for duration (yes).
- Latency: target is to demonstrate <=60ms p95 on their traces in spike; committing to <=50ms p95 in SOW requires an explicit cost add-on for dedicated infra + a short engineering engagement to do kernel-level tuning.

Blockers / risks:
- Scheduling on dedicated HW (we can reserve but it impacts other commitments).
- If Suncrest requires hard SLA at day 1 of pilot, we should push to have a short performance validation window before SOW signature or build language that SLO is a target post-acceptance.

I'll draft a two-week spike plan (engineer_spike_plan.md) and attach. If leadership agrees, we can spin up nodes next week.

—Dev

Thanks Dev — this is helpful and pragmatic. Recap and next steps so we have alignment for procurement/SOW language:

1) We can offer residency via a short-term Dedicated pool (confirmed). I will add explicit wording to the SOW that the pilot includes "dedicated node tenancy for pilot tenant" with expected node counts listed as pending engineering confirmation.
2) For latency, we will present 60ms p95 as the initial engineering-backed target from the spike. If Suncrest wants contractual 50ms p95, we will attach a costed addendum that covers the extra infra + kernel tuning engagement.

Action items and owners:
- Dev: finalize spike plan and target perf report by Aug 29 (engineer_spike_plan.md attached).
- Karthik/Product: draft the SOW language variations (baseline + 50ms addendum) by Aug 25.
- Marissa/SE: prepare a short playbook for onboarding (warmup scripts, recommended prompt prefixes) to maximize KV cache hit.
- Ben/AE: hold the procurement thread and update Suncrest by Aug 25 with go/no-go and cost addendum option.

Sam — copying you so this is transparent. We will confirm by Aug 25 whether we can accept the SOW as-is or will need an addendum for the 50ms contractual SLA. If you can confirm flexibility on either the SLO or budget for a dedicated tuning engagement, that will help speed things up.

Neha
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
